summary: Yasuo Sano is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied under Kenyu Mitomo (attested 1996) and founded the Buha Bukkyo Shiso Kenkyukai.

Yasuo Yuasa (1925–2005) worked in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Tetsuro Watsuji and held posts at Tokyo, Yamanashi, Osaka, Tsukuba (1981–1989), and J. F. Oberlin University (emeritus, 1989).

Yasuro Abe (born 1953) is a scholar of Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Wako and Otani Universities, he served at Osaka, Otemae, Nagoya (professor 1998, emeritus 2000–2019), and Ryukoku University (2019).

Yasusaburo Sakaki (1870–1929) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. After studying at the University of Tokyo (c. 1895–1899), he held academic posts at the University of Tokyo (c. 1899–1903) and Kyushu University (c. 1906–1928).

Yasushi Endo is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He held academic posts at Nagoya University, Aichi Bunkyo University (attested 2000–2004), and Shitennoji University as a professor (attested 2000).

Yasutaka Muroya is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He was a project research associate at the University of Vienna (attested 2007) and University of Leipzig (attested 2015), and a research associate at IKGA (attested 2016–2022).

Yasutoshi Murakami (born 1941) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University (c. 1960–1969). He held posts at Yamaguchi University (c. 1970–1989) and Koyasan University (c. 1989–2012), and led the Association of Esoteric Buddhist Studies (attested 2004).
Yawen Yang is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed an MA at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Yongdong Shi (attested 2009).

Yelena Rudenko works in Indology and history/archaeology. She studied at Al-Farabi Kazakh National University, the University of Delhi, and R. B. Suleimenov Institute of Oriental Studies, later working as a research fellow at the Suleimenov Institute (2006–2019).

Yellava Subbarayalu (born 1940) specializes in history, archaeology, and Indology. He has served as a professor at Tamil University and as a researcher at the French Institute of Pondicherry (attested 2015).
Yeshe Thupten is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. In 1982, he held appointments at Middlebury College and as a visiting scholar at the University of Virginia.

Yeshi Donden (1927–2019) worked in Tibetology and traditional medicine. He studied at the Chakpori Institute of Tibetan Medicine under Khyenrab Norbu, and he founded the Men-Tsee-Khang in 1961, serving as its director from 1961 to 1966.
Yi-hsun Huang is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who completed a PhD at the University of Virginia under the supervision of Paul Groner (attested 2001).

Yifa (born 1959) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at National Taiwan University, University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, and Yale University under Stanley Weinstein. She held posts at University of the West and Harvard, and founded the Woodenfish Foundation.
Yifan Zhang works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology, serving as both a PhD student and a faculty member at Ghent University (attested 2026).

Yigal Bronner is an Indologist who studied at Hebrew University of Jerusalem and the University of Chicago under Sheldon Pollock. He was appointed associate professor at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem around 2010.

Yijie Tang (1927–2014) was a scholar of philosophy, sinology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Peking University (c. 1947–1951), he served as a professor there (c. 1956–2014) and founded the International Academy of Chinese Culture.

Yiliang Zhou (1913–2001) worked in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He studied at Fu Jen, Yenching, and Harvard, studied under Yinke Chen, and served as a professor at Peking University (c. 1952–2001).
Yiling Hua specializes in Tibetology and history/archaeology. She completed a PhD at Waseda University (2020–2024) and joined Kunming University of Science and Technology as a lecturer in 2024.

Ying-Kuang Chu (1883–1973) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Hangzhou Chicheng Public School. His traditional teachers included Nordan Hutuktu, Nona Hutuktu, Bai Puren, and Gangkar Rinpoche.
